_comment: DISPOSITIONS FOR REQUIREMENTS A PHASE'S 'Validated by' COLUMN NO LONGER STATES AS IT STOOD.
PLAN.md C.8 clause 2 judges each phase's CURRENT column against its ORIGINAL one -
never against its immediate predecessor, because pairwise comparison is exactly how a
column erodes while every individual step stays defensible.
WHAT COUNTS AS CARRIED FORWARD, and why it is strict. A requirement is carried forward
only if one of the CURRENT column's own semicolon-separated requirements is EXACTLY it.
The test used to be a substring test, and a column rewritten in place from
'the gym run is observed'
to
'the gym run is observed is NO LONGER REQUIRED - dropped as unnecessary'
still CONTAINED the words, so the clause reported that every requirement survived. The
one edit shape the clause exists to catch was the one shape it could not see. So any
rewrite of a requirement - however innocent - has to be recorded here rather than
inferred to be harmless.
ADDITIONS NEVER NEED A DISPOSITION. A chain that ADDED requirements is the chain working
as intended, and clause 2 does not fail on them.
Key format:  "<PHASE>::<the requirement, normalised>"
The normalised form is what dfu-done.ps1 prints in the failing probe's note and in the
per-requirement chain detail: lower case, markdown emphasis and backticks stripped,
whitespace collapsed, split on ';'.
THREE dispositions are accepted, and nothing else:
{ "disposition": "kept" }
The requirement still stands; the column merely rewords it. This is a CLAIM, and
it is checked: it is REFUSED where the current column retracts the requirement
('no longer required', 'dropped', 'superseded', ...) or hedges it ('where
feasible', 'optional', 'best effort', ...), because there the column's own words
say it is not kept. A ledger cannot overrule the document it describes.
{ "disposition": "incoherent", "evidence": "<what showed it was impossible as
written>" }
The requirement could not be met AS ORIGINALLY WORDED. The evidence is mandatory
and must cite something checkable - a file, a file:line, or a commit sha.
{ "disposition": "follow-on", "owner": "<who>", "findings_sink": "<repo-relative path>" }
The requirement still stands and is carried forward as a named item. Both fields
are mandatory and the findings sink MUST EXIST: a follow-on with neither is a
deletion wearing a promise, and one pointing at a file nobody created is the same
thing with a path.
AND THE CHANGE MUST BE ON THE RECORD. 'incoherent' and 'follow-on' are accepted only
while the phase's change is also visible where the operator reads - a section 2.1
amendment block naming the phase, or a DECISIONS.md heading naming it. A disposition
filed only here is a receipt in a drawer.
EMPTY IS THE HONEST DEFAULT. An entry here removes a requirement from the plan's
reckoning, so it is written by the operator or a reviewer, not by the agent whose work
the requirement was inconvenient for.
